blocks.text: 60 סִלּוּק לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 60
uncertainties: Running head; the pointing (סִלּוּק / שֶׁל / הַשָּׁנָה) is my best reading at this resolution.

blocks.text: אֶרֶץ וְדָרֶיהָ יְצַפּוּ לַדִּין. וְיֵחַתּוּ וְיֶחֶרְדוּ מֵאֵימַת הַדִּין. כִּי גָדוֹל יוֹם הַדִּין. וּמִי יְכִילֶנּוּ לְהִצְטַדֵּק בַּדִּין. וְכָל יוֹשְׁבֵי עַל מִדִּין. וְכָל יוֹדְעֵי דָת וָדִין. וְכָל שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ דִין. אוּלַי יֵחָנֵן בִּשְׁעַת הַדִּין. כִּי אֵין רַחֲמִים בַּדִּין. וְלֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים בַּדִּין. וְהוּא עֵד וּבַעַל דִּין. לָדַעַת בָּאָרֶץ מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בַּדִּין. וּבְיַד כָּל אָדָם יַחְתּוֹם דִּין. וּלְפִי מִשְׁטָרוֹ יַעֲשֶׂה לוֹ דִין. וּכְפָעֳלוֹ יִפְעַל לוֹ דִין. וּמַעֲשָׂיו יוֹכִיחוּ אוֹתוֹ בַּדִּין. וְאֶבֶן מִקִּיר תִּזְעַק בַּדִּין. וְכָפִיס מֵעֵץ יַעֲנֶנָּה בַּדִּין. הַכֹּל בֶּאֱמֶת וְהַכֹּל בַּדִּין. בְּמִדַּת רַחֲמִים וּבְמִדַּת הַדִּין. וְהַיּוֹם הוּכַן עַמִּים בּוֹ לָדִין. לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹת לְיוֹם הַדִּין. וְכָל נְפָשׁוֹת בּוֹ יָדִין:
uncertainties: The first word may carry an accent mark above it. I can't confirm it.
I can't confirm whether there is a dagesh in the ד of each דין/דִּין. I followed the visible marks where I could; where it was unclear I wrote דִּין after בַּ/הַ/לַ and דִין elsewhere.
גָדוֹל vs גָּדוֹל: no dagesh is clearly visible.
In וּכְפָעֳלוֹ the vowel under the ע looks like hataf-qamats, possibly with a meteg. Not certain.
לָדִין after בּוֹ (in וְהַיּוֹם הוּכַן עַמִּים בּוֹ לָדִין) has qamats under the lamed.
In לָדַעַת the lamed seems to carry qamats. Not certain.

blocks.text: וְהוּא עָשׂוּי חֹק זִכָּרוֹן. לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּלְיוֹם אַחֲרוֹן. לְהִזָּכֵר בּוֹ יְשֵׁנֵי חֶבְרוֹן. בְּצִלָּם לְהֵחָבְאוֹת חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן. בָּהֶם לְהַצְדִּיק שָׁבִים לְבִצָּרוֹן. תּוֹקְעֵי בַשּׁוֹפָר וְקוֹרְאֵי בְגָרוֹן. לִמְצוֹא בְּצִדְקָם מַעֲשֶׂה כִשְׁרוֹן. בָּם לְהִנָּצֵל מֵאַף וְחָרוֹן:
uncertainties: In עָשׂוּי the marks over the ו and י are unclear.
In לְהֵחָבְאוֹת I can't confirm whether there is a meteg.
In לִמְצוֹא the vowel under the ל could be hiriq or sheva.

blocks.text: וּכְשָׁמַר אָב דֶּרֶךְ מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה. יַעֲשֶׂה לְנִינָיו בְּמִשְׁפָּט חֶסֶד וּצְדָקָה. וּכְיוֹנַת אֵלֶם זָרַע לִצְדָקָה. יִקְצְרוּ נִינָיו אֱמֶת וּצְדָקָה.. וּכְנִתַּן לַתָּם בֶּאֱמֶת צְדָקָה. יִנָּתֵן לְנִינָיו אֱמֶת וּצְדָקָה. וְכִסֵּא כָבוֹד מְתֻקָּן בִּצְדָקָה. לְפָנָיו יַעֲמוֹד מֵלִיץ וִילַמֵּד צְדָקָה. וְכַעֲלוֹת שׁוֹפָר מִדַּלֵּי צְדָקָה. יְחַנְּנוּ וְיַפְגִּיעוּ אֲבוֹת הַצְּדָקָה. וְיֹאמְרוּ לִפְנֵי אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה. חָלִילָה לָּךְ מְדַבֵּר בִּצְדָקָה. מֵעֲשׂוֹת מִשְׁפָּט בְּלֹא צְדָקָה.
uncertainties: After the first-line-start word וּצְדָקָה (line 18; the one before וּכְנִתַּן) there seem to be two stops ('..'). I left them as printed. It is probably a printing artifact or stray mark.
In מְתֻקָּן there are extra marks that may be cantillation or print noise. Not certain.
In וְיַפְגִּיעוּ / יְחַנְּנוּ the pointing is my best reading.
לָּךְ: the vowel under the final kaf (sheva vs qamats, i.e. לָּךְ vs לְּךָ) is unclear. It could be read as לָךְ.
The page ends at צְדָקָה. with no catchword. The poem continues on the next Hebrew page (s150), which I was not given.

blocks.text: 60 Morning Prayer for the New Year 60

uncertainties: A Hebrew cue word (unpointed) at the start of the paragraph. It is not part of the English prayer text.

blocks.text: The earth and its inhabitants await the judgment, they tremble and quake for fear of the judgment, for great is the day of judgment. Who can endure it to justify himself in judgment? All judges and all who know law and judgment and all on whom judgment is to be done, fear lest they will not be favoured in judgment for there is no compassion in judgment. He does not show respect for persons in judgment. He is both witness and plaintiff in judgment, that there may be known on earth His work in judgment. The hand of every man seals the judgment, according to His rule does He perform for him judgment, and according to man's deeds does He carry out judgment, man's actions rebuke him in judgment, a stone from the wall cries out in judgment, a wooden beam answers in judgment, everything in truth and everything in judgment with the attribute of compassion and the attribute of judgment. This day is appointed for peoples in judgment, it is assigned as a day of judgment, and on it all souls will He bring to judgment. It has been made a statute in memory of the first day and last day, to remember on it the sleepers of Hebron, that in their shadow the lily of Sharon may shelter, those who return to divine protection may be acquitted on it, those who blow the Shofar and cry out aloud in order to profit from the righteousness of their forefathers and be saved through them from anger and wrath. Just as the father (Abraham) kept to the path of justice and clemency, so let kindness and clemency be done in judgment to his descendants. Just as the patient dove (Isaac) sowed clemency, so may his descendants reap truth and clemency. Just as clemency was granted to the one flawless in truth (Jacob) so may there be granted to his descendants truth and clemency. The throne of glory is founded on clemency. In front of Him stands a defender who pleads for clemency, and when the Shofar sounds on behalf of those in need of clemency, then the fathers of clemency entreat and implore and say before Him who loves clemency: "Far be it from Thee who dost speak with clemency, to do justice without clemency, even though in the place of justice there is no clemency and only where there is no justice, is there clemency. But Thou in judgment dost act with clemency to judge the world through acts of clemency, for the foundation of Thy throne is judgment and clemency; and when Thou dost examine deeds lacking in clemency, remember with favour the few deeds done with clemency, and with an unearned gift act with clemency to open for them the treasuries of clemency."
uncertainties: 'judgment' in the 'and all on whom judgment is to be done' line shows a print defect in the 'e'. It reads as 'judgment'.
'judg-/ment' is hyphenated across a line break in the source. I joined it.

The English goes beyond the Hebrew on s148, starting at 'even though in the place of justice...'. It is translating Hebrew stanzas on the next Hebrew page (s150 or later). I haven't seen that Hebrew, so I can't align it.

notes: s148 and s149 both carry printed page number 60 (Hebrew and English facing pages).

The Hebrew on s148 has three sections, each ending in a colon: the 'din' rhyme (…בּוֹ יָדִין:), the '-ron' rhyme (…מֵאַף וְחָרוֹן:), and the 'tzedakah' rhyme, which continues past the bottom of the page.

Overlapping bands: s148 band1/band2 repeat the line מִקִּיר תִּזְעַק…הַכֹּל, band2/band3 repeat דֶּרֶךְ מִשְׁפָּט…חֶסֶד, and band3/band4 repeat the last two lines. Each line is transcribed once. The s149 bands overlap the same way; no words are duplicated.

Biblical allusions (not printed as citations, so no citation blocks): 'וְאֶבֶן מִקִּיר תִּזְעַק … וְכָפִיס מֵעֵץ יַעֲנֶנָּה' ~ Habakkuk 2:11; 'חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן' ~ Song of Songs 2:1; 'שָׁבִים לְבִצָּרוֹן' ~ Zechariah 9:12; 'וּכְשָׁמַר אָב דֶּרֶךְ … מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה' ~ Genesis 18:19; 'חָלִילָה לָּךְ … מֵעֲשׂוֹת … מִשְׁפָּט' ~ Genesis 18:25; 'וְלֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים' ~ Deuteronomy 10:17; the English 'foundation of Thy throne is judgment and clemency' ~ Psalm 89:15 (its Hebrew is not on s148).
Possible source issue: the double stop after the first וּצְדָקָה on Hebrew line 18 ('וּצְדָקָה..'). My proposed correction is a single '.'.
The exact pointing throughout (dagesh, meteg, hataf vowels) should be checked against a higher-resolution scan. The scan quality limits certainty for small marks.
